Cover is dressed. He wears a coat, waistcoat, and trousers, and has boots upon his feet. He is bareheaded, and has no other covering upon his head. He is young, and has the appearance of being in good health. He is not remarkable in any way, and has no peculiarity of dress. He is a native of England, and has no other language than his own. He is a shoemaker by trade, and has never been out of Europe. He has never been in any kind of covering, except dress.

I am a spirit, and have existed from all eternity. In the beginning I was with God. I am immortal, and can never die. The heaven is my abiding place, and the earth is my footstool. I am invisible to the natural eye, but I am seen by the eye of faith. I am distinct from matter, and can have no fellowship with it. Spiritually I am married to Christ, and my business is to bear witness of him to the world.
You are happy, because you are dead.

I am a ghost. I appear to certain persons, in order togratify their wishes, and to enable them to discover things future or secret. I can also appear of my own free will, and for purposes of amusement. In the former case, my power extends no further than to gratify the curiosity of the person I love; in the latter, I can assume any shape, and exert any degree of influence. I can render myself visible, or invisible, at pleasure; and I can pass through walls, and enter into closed rooms. By these means I have been enabled to procure great riches, and to gratify ardent affection. I have appeared to many, and never failed to fulfil the expectations of any. I am steam. When power is wanted, I can furnish it. I can drive machinery, and I can light houses and buildings with brilliancy. I can transport a great many persons speedily and cheaply, and I can warm houses comfortably. In short, I can furnish power.

I am the ninth edition of the first book published in Scotland, being the first edition of the Psalms of David in metre, printed at Edinburgh in the year 1560, in the reign of the first king of Scotland of the house of Stuart. I am commonly called the first edition of the first Scottish Psalms, and in the later editions I am styled the first part of the first edition. I was published in the year immediately following the establishment of the Reformation in Scotland, and in the very earliest period of the art of printing in the kingdom. I was published in the time of the first and second editions of the first English book, commonly called Matthew’s Bible, and in the first year of the publication of the first German Protestant edition of the Holy Scriptures.
